extracted.intended_audience: aspiring poets/writers and general readers of moral fiction
extracted.subtask_description: Moral and ethical guidance for poets/writers embedded in literary narrative; advises how creative power should be used and what temptations to resist (wealth, pandering, corrupting influence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtue as the sinew of true genius
rubrics_metrics.description: "Virtue ... is ever the sinew of true genius. Together, the two in one, they are endow'd with immortal strength, and approach loftily to Him from whom both spring."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text argues that moral integrity (virtue) is an essential component of genuine artistic genius; poetic power divorced from virtue is deficient. Treat virtue not as optional ornament but as structural support for lasting creative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware how you use intellectual power; avoid furthering bad ends
rubrics_metrics.description: "Let the man to whom the great Master has given the might of mind, beware how he uses that might. If for the furtherance of bad ends, what can be expected but that... thoughts of harm done... will come and swarm like spectres around him?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creators should consider the moral consequences of their output: even a jesting falsehood or a casually propagated bad principle can have large, harmful social effects ("a bad principle, jestingly spoken--a falsehood, but of a word--may taint a whole nation!"). Avoid using talent to promote vice or degrade humanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer integrity and poverty over corrupt prosperity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Be and continue poor, young man... Be without place and power, while others beg their way upward. Bear the pain of disappointed hopes, while others gain the accomplishment of their flattery. Forego the gracious pressure of a hand, for which others cringe and crawl. Wrap yourself in your own virtue... If you have... grown gray with unblench'd honor, bless God and die."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author counsels writers to choose honor and uncorrupted principle over material success achieved by compromise. This is prescriptive: decline remunerations or commissions that require betraying conscience or promoting unholy aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resist envy and worldly ambition; maintain intellectual independence
rubrics_metrics.description: "Do justice, philosopher, to your own powers. While the world runs after its shadows and its bubbles... we will fold ourselves in our circle of understanding, and look with an eye of apathy on those things it considers so mighty and so enviable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let envy of wealth, status, or fashionable life divert a writer from pursuing their own intellectual and artistic path. Cultivate detachment from worldly pomp and pursue work valued by discerning peers rather than mass applause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pandering to the vulgar; preserve refined standards
rubrics_metrics.description: "Our intellect would be sullied, were the vulgar to approximate to it, by professing to readily enter in, and praising it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text warns against lowering standards to please popular taste. Maintain refined standards in language, thought, and moral stance; avoid writing that sacrifices depth and integrity for easy popular approbation.
